metadata.generator: text-to-robot design engine (real components + printed structure)
notes: Interpreted locally: type inferred, DOF=4, gripper=parallel.
metadata.source_prompt: An Arduino 4WD obstacle avoiding car with an ultrasonic sensor

design.summary: Arduino car (stronger (4WD, ramps up to 10 deg)): 4WD on TT gear motors, 0.53 kg, 0.54 m/s, 99 min, $37 of parts

uses: plug-in wiring for the board and driver

checks.name: clearance:home
checks.detail: no printed part or component intersects another

checks.name: drive:torque
checks.detail: 0.53 kg on a 10 deg slope accelerating 0.5 m/s^2: 0.0171 N·m per wheel (incl. 0.0063 gearbox loss at speed) vs 0.0235 N·m continuous (TT 1:48)

checks.name: drive:top_speed
checks.detail: 0.54 m/s at 6 V (no-load 20.944 rad/s x r 32.5 mm x 0.8)

checks.name: power:driver_current
checks.detail: one TT motor per TB6612FNG channel: stall 1.5 A <= 3.2 A channel peak (1.2 A continuous)

checks.name: power:motor_voltage
checks.detail: 2S pack 6.0-8.4 V through the TB6612FNG: the sketch caps PWM at 182/255 so the 6 V motors never see more than 6 V average

checks.name: power:runtime
checks.detail: 99 min driving (9.0 W average from 18.5 Wh, 80 % usable)

performance.controller: Arduino Nano compatible board (ATmega328P, CH340, USB-C)

assumptions: TT motor continuous torque taken as 30 % of the 0.8 kg.cm stall (Adafruit #3777 data)
prices are typical single-unit marketplace prices for generic modules and vary by seller
